# Instructions for AI assistants working on SillyDES

## The documents say what is known now

Every document says what is known now: README.md, SECURITY.md, STRUCTURE.md, TESTING.md, ANALYSIS.md,
every section of CHANGELOG.md, and the comments in the code. Do not refer to, correct or argue with what
an earlier text said.

- Do not write "earlier revisions said", "was given as", "is now", "no longer", "corrected", "superseded",
  "withdrawn", "reassessed", "contrary to" or "than stated", and do not add a section or a list that says
  how the conclusions changed.
- When a figure or a finding changes, replace it in place in every document that names it, the sections of
  released versions in CHANGELOG.md included. The text must read as if it had always said so. Search all
  documents for the old figure before you finish.
- The changelog says what a release contains and what it changes in the program and its files. It does not
  say what a document claimed before.
- Where a measurement comes from (which release, which tool) is a fact, not history. It stays, in section 14
  of ANALYSIS.md.
- In your answers to the user you may say what you changed. In the files you may not.

The same rule for maintainers is in STRUCTURE.md, section 10. Keep the two in step.
